    Here’s The Setlist For KATSEYE’s WILDWORLD Tour

    By Madison MurraySeptember 2, 2026No Comments2 Mins Read
    Share
    Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Pinterest Email
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 1:49
    Instaread

    Things are about to get WILD for KATSEYE fans! After wowing us with their latest EP, WILD, the girls officially kicked off their WILDWORLD Tour in Dublin on September 1st. They’re doing this live run as a four-piece so far – Manon is still on hiatus and Sophia is taking some time away for her health – but we know that Daniela, Lara, Megan, and Yoonchae will light up every single stage they step on during this tour. Each member even gets a solo section to shine on their own!

    Arzt | Side | Belek | Antalya | Hausarzt

    The tour will hit countries like England and France during the European run before heading to North America to stop in cities like Miami, FL and Los Angeles, CA. Finally, the girls will wrap things up in Mexico City at the end of November, then they’ll hopefully get some well-deserved rest and time to reflect on all their hard work!

    Arzt | Side | Belek | Antalya | Hausarzt
    visit belekarzt.com/ to learn more

    Here’s the setlist for KATSEYE’s WILDWORLD Tour as of the first show in Dublin, Ireland: 

    • ‘Hootie Frutti’
    • ‘Internet Girl’
    • ‘That Way’
    • ‘Touch’
    • ‘Mean Girls’
    • Daniela Solo: Dance 
    • ‘Gabriela’
    • ‘PINKY UP’
    • Megan Solo: Dance
    • ‘Animal’
    • ‘Tonight I Might’
    • ‘I’m Pretty’
    • ‘Time Lapse’
    • ‘Gameboy’
    • Lara Solo: ‘Unloveu’
    • ‘My Way’
    • ‘Bel Air’
    • Yoonchae Solo: Dance 
    • ‘M.I.A’
    • ‘Debut’
    • ‘ICONIC BY MISTAKE’
    • ‘Gnarly’

    What do you think of the WILDWORLD Tour setlist, Eyekons? Do you have your tickets to see KATSEYE live this year? Let us know in the comments below or hit us up on Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter! You can also buzz on over to our Reddit community to chat with us.

    The Fray Turned Sterling Heights Into One Big Glowing Singalong And We’re Still Recovering

    By Asia M.September 2, 2026No Comments5 Mins Read
    Share
    Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Pinterest Email

    There’s a specific kind of magic that happens when a band you grew up with walks back onstage and somehow sounds bigger than you remembered. That’s exactly what went down when The Fray rolled into the Michigan Lottery Amphitheatre at Freedom Hill, bringing their Summer of Light Tour to a very willing Michigan crowd. Cool night, open-air amphitheater, a few thousand people who knew every word. You already know how this ends. Everyone left a little hoarse.

    We came in ready for nostalgia. What we didn’t fully expect was how much it would actually heal something. If you grew up on these songs, seeing them performed live for the first time hits differently, a little bittersweet, a lot overwhelming, the kind of thing that catches in your throat before you even realize why. So let’s talk about it.

    The Vibe Walking In

    Freedom Hill has this way of feeling both massive and weirdly intimate at the same time, and that suited The Fray perfectly. The lighting leaned into that golden hour that never ends feeling, all warm ambers and soft spotlights that made the whole stage glow like a memory you’re trying to hold onto. Fitting especially for a tour literally themed around light. The band shares this run with Dashboard Confessional and Colony House, which is a lineup practically engineered to make anyone who came of age in the 2000s completely lose it. By the time The Fray took over, the amphitheater was buzzing. That low hum of a crowd that knows it’s about to get everything it paid for!

    A New Voice For Songs You Know By Heart

    Here’s the thing about The Fray live. Their whole sound is built on that push and pull between piano-driven tenderness and full-band catharsis, and that translates so well to a stage this size. One minute you’re swaying to something soft and aching, the next the whole band leans in and the drums crack open and suddenly everyone’s on their feet. Ben Wysocki especially was a joy to watch, locked in and grinning through the bigger moments, sticks flying during the heavier build-ups. And Joe King worked every inch of that stage, dropping to his knees during the emotional peaks, arms flung wide during the anthems, hyping the crowd like he genuinely could not believe how loud Michigan was willing to get. Spoiler: very loud!

    Wait, Was That A Mirror?

    Okay, we need a whole moment for this. At one point the Joe pulled out this genuinely stunning bit of stagecraft using a mirror and light, bouncing beams around the amphitheater in a way that felt almost handmade compared to the usual wall-of-LEDs approach so many tours lean on now. It was simple and gorgeous and completely on theme. The kind of effect that makes you gasp a little and then immediately turn to whoever you came with. For a Summer of Light Tour, it was the perfect visual thesis statement.

    The Songs That Made Everyone Lose It

    You want the hits? They delivered the hits. ‘Over My Head (Cable Car)’ was an early gut-punch of joy, the kind of song that instantly transports you back to being a teenager with earbuds in and too many feelings. ‘Never Say Never’ absolutely wrecked us in the best way, all swelling piano and that ache in the chorus that hits harder when a whole amphitheater is holding it up with you. And then there’s the one-two punch of ‘You Found Me’ and ‘How To Save A Life.’ Those opening piano notes triggered that instant pavlovian gasp across the lawn, and the singalong got so loud the band could’ve stepped back and let the crowd carry entire choruses. A few times, they basically did. Hearing these songs live after growing up with them on repeat? That’s the part that healed something. No notes!

    What really got us, though, was how the newer material held its own. The Summer of Light run has been folding in fresh songs alongside the classics, and instead of being the moment everyone runs for the bathroom, those newer tracks fit right into the emotional arc. That’s not always a given for a band with this deep a nostalgia pull. It says something about where they’re at creatively right now.

    Was It Worth It?

    Short answer, absolutely! Longer answer, this was one of those shows that reminds you why live music matters in the first place. The kind of night where strangers make eye contact mid-chorus because you’re both feeling the exact same thing. The band sounded tight, the crowd was fully invested, and that summer-night amphitheater energy did the rest. If this tour is coming anywhere near you, we hope you got a chance to attend.

    What did you think of The Fray’s Summer of Light? Were you there singing your heart out with us? Let us know on Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram!
